headline: I build practical AI systems,
from intelligent pipelines
to experiences people
can actually use.
intro: I'm Aasveer, a Computer Science & Engineering (AI/ML) student who enjoys building practical applications that bring intelligent systems, backend engineering, data processing and usable interfaces together.

perspective.note: A way of looking at a problem, not the architecture of any one project.

stages.label: Problem
stages.explanation: Start with what a person is actually trying to do, and what a useful result would look like, before choosing any tools.

stages.label: Intelligence
stages.explanation: Choose the technique that fits the problem, whether that is retrieval, language understanding, ranking or a language model.

stages.label: Engineering
stages.explanation: Build what surrounds the model: the data processing, backend services and APIs that let it run as a real application.

stages.label: Experience
stages.explanation: Bring it to an interface someone can use, because that is where all of the other work becomes useful.

principles.label: Practical AI
principles.text: I enjoy building practical applications that use AI to address real problems rather than treating models as isolated demonstrations.

principles.label: Systems Thinking
principles.text: I am interested in bringing together intelligent systems, data processing, backend engineering, APIs and user-facing interfaces.

principles.label: Human-Centred Engineering
principles.text: The usefulness of an intelligent system depends on how well its different components work together for the person using it.

process.note: A way of thinking more than a fixed recipe. Every project moves through these differently.

stages.label: Understand the problem
stages.explanation: Work out what the person actually needs and what a good result looks like, before choosing any tools.

example.text: The real risk was a model inventing gifts that don't exist, so ranking real catalogue items became the core of the design.

stages.label: Design the system
stages.explanation: Decide what the parts are, what each one is responsible for, and how data moves between them.

example.text: One Python core holds every rule, so the command-line app and the web app cannot disagree.

stages.label: Build the pipeline
stages.explanation: Build the main path one stage at a time, so each step can be checked on its own.

example.text: A screenshot passes through OCR, signal analysis, profiling and retrieval as separate stages.

stages.label: Connect the components
stages.explanation: Join the backend, data and interface through clear boundaries, so one part can change without breaking the rest.

example.text: An Express and Vite server proxies API calls to FastAPI, so the browser talks to a single origin.

stages.label: Test and refine
stages.explanation: Try real inputs, see what breaks, and plan for what happens when a dependency isn't there.

example.text: Without a Gemini key, the app shows the retrieved source text and labels it clearly, instead of failing.
